hook.text: Sildenafil and tadalafil don't create an erection. They stop your body from switching one off.

vessel.text: An erection is a blood flow event. Inside the penis, two spongy chambers are fed by arteries wrapped in smooth muscle. At rest, that muscle stays tense, and the arteries stay narrow.

signal.text: With arousal, nerves and the vessel lining release nitric oxide. It slips into the muscle cells and switches on an enzyme that makes a messenger molecule called cyclic G M P.

relax.text: Cyclic G M P tells the muscle to relax. Calcium inside the cell drops, the arteries widen, blood fills the chambers, and the swelling squeezes the exit veins shut.

pde5.text: But the body always builds in an off switch. An enzyme called P D E 5 chops cyclic G M P into an inactive fragment, and the signal fades.

inhibit.text: Sildenafil and tadalafil are P D E 5 inhibitors. They compete for the enzyme's active site, so cyclic G M P is broken down more slowly, and the relaxation signal lasts longer.

timing.text: Nothing starts without stimulation, because no nitric oxide means no signal to protect. The big difference is time. Sildenafil's half-life is about four hours. Tadalafil's is about seventeen.

safety.text: These drugs also widen other blood vessels, which is why mixing them with nitrate medicines can drop blood pressure dangerously. Same enzyme, same vessels, different timing.
